newsitem.title: USA: Lebed firing will not upset Russia debt rating - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Lebed firing will not upset Russia debt rating - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Thursday said its BB-minus Russian foreign currency debt rating is not under pressure from President Boris Yeltsin's surprise ouster of national security chief Alexander Lebed.

"If something like that would affect our rating, then our rating would be worth nothing," said Helena Hessel, director of S&P's sovereign ratings group. "Our rating is not based on whether Lebed is security chief or not."
Hessel said the agency has already factored in event risk far greater than the Lebed firing.
"Our rating would stand even if Yeltsin should die," she said. "Even under the worst case scenario (of Communist leader Gennady) Zyuganov coming back, the rating would stand."

In a conference call one week ago, Hessel had said that a short period of stress in Russia would not affect the country's debt service ability or lead the agency to downgrade the country's debt rating.
Hessel said prolonged stresses between Russia and the International Monetary Fund could force a ratings cut, however.
